summary:
Small source-only research product closing two suspicions and keeping the frontier current; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics. No map change is proposed, so the accepted map stays at its current version and every accepted result keeps its basis.

Closed leads, with sources: (1) the protocol-version gate cannot underflow at the minimum. checkRPCHeader rejects when header.ProtocolVersion < r.config().ProtocolVersion-1 (raft.go:60-70), which would have meant a node at ProtocolVersionMin rejecting every peer if the comparison wrapped; it does not, because ProtocolVersion is a signed int (config.go:99, Min 0 / Max 3), so the expression is -1 at the minimum and no valid header is rejected. This also confirms the gate the heartbeat fast path skips is a genuine bounded window, strengthening rather than weakening that finding. (2) liveBootstrap cannot bootstrap a node that already has state despite forcing the term to 1 and setting the last log from the bootstrap entry, because BootstrapCluster refuses when HasExistingState reports state (api.go:252-259) and the path is only reachable through the bootstrap channel on an un-bootstrapped node.

New sources recorded: S60 (config.go version constants) and S61 (api.go BootstrapCluster). The feedback references existing objects only (S42, b-append-entries-sync, b-heartbeat-fast-path), so no new graph objects were invented and no version was created.

Frontier left explicitly open: the ReloadConfig lease-timer lead; the processHeartbeat concurrency contract; the deployment-level premises behind the four confirmed findings (real reachability of an unconfigured TimeoutNow sender, the election consequence of a fast-path heartbeat, whether batching FSMs are exempt from ConfigurationStore, and how long a snapshot-installed tail persists under a live leader); and the still-unread observer plumbing, snapshot-store implementations, and net_transport beyond the heartbeat classification.
